sentences.text: Aktaua is an extinct genus of sawfish belonging to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish like sharks and rays.
This creature is placed within the family Myliobatidae, a group that typically includes stingrays and their relatives.
The genus Aktaua is known from only one species, Aktaua kizylkumensis, found in the White Mountain Formation in Uzbekistan.
The species name kizylkumensis refers to the Kizylkum Desert, while the genus name Aktaua comes from the Uzbek word for 'white,' describing the color of the rock formation.
There is only one recorded fossil occurrence of Aktaua in the Paleobiology Database, and the genus was described by Case and colleagues in 1996.
These animals lived between 48.07 and 41.03 million years ago during the Lutetian stage of the Eocene epoch.
